To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the serum concentration of MMP‐3 is lower in patients with acute MI than in healthy subjects and that the MMP‐3 5A allele is associated with a lower concentration of serum MMP‐3.
the serum level of MMP‐3 is decreased in the acute phase after MI and the −1612A allele of the MMP‐3 gene is associated with lower serum levels of MMP‐3.
MMP-3 is a potential marker of acute MI, and that the MMP-3 5A allele is associated with higher risk of acute MI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: Is the serum concentration of MMP‐3 increased in the acute stage after MI?

the role of MMP‐3, which is a key enzyme in the degradation of the extracellular matrix, in the acute stage (within the first 24 h after the onset of symptoms) of MI, and the influence of MMP‐3 promoter polymorphism (−1612 5 A/6 A ) on serum concentration of MMP‐3 and the risk of acute MI.
the role of MMP‐3 and MMP‐3 promoter polymorphism in the development of coronary artery disease and acute myocardial infarct.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a 3D model is a good way of assessing the effects of the different factors that can influence the performance of the system.
the use of the MMP‐3 gene polymorphism in the prediction of MI is of no value.
the MMP‐3 gene polymorphism is a risk factor for the development of coronary artery disease and myocardial infarctions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the acute phase after myocardial infarct the concentration of MMP‐3 is lower than in the control group and the 5A/5A genotype is associated with higher serum concentration of MMP‐ 3 than 6A/6A.
the MMP‐3 gene polymorphism is a risk factor for MI and a low serum concentration of MMP‐3 is a marker of MI.
MMP‐3 is a useful biomarker for the acute phase of MI and that the 5A allele is associated with a decreased risk of acute MI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a new role for a well‐known protein in the pathophysiology of aortic dissection, which is that MMP‐3 is involved in the regulation of aortic smooth muscle cell proliferation.
the 5A/5A MMP‐3 genotype is associated with a higher risk of cardiovascular events and that the MMP‐3 5A/−1612A allele has a negative impact on survival in patients with acute myocardial infarctions.
MMP‐3 may be a marker of plaque stability and rupture.
